items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1963-03-28
items.q: There wasn't nobody but me and Bill, my granddaddy and my aunt. Because he taught, you know, his teachings.

ctx.x: of Earl Humphrey, Moetze 28th 1963. I'd just like to have it on the tape. In case we get the box mixed up. You were telling me about the bass. You took up the bass huh? Yeah. You couldn't make money huh?

No, well I didn't. Family bass. We had the rehearsal every Friday. There wasn't nobody but me and Bill, my granddaddy and my aunt. Because he taught, you know, his teachings. Neighborhood children come down there like T.V. Thomas, Eric Williams, and that big, big town at the, when out of California was healthy and died out there. In our front room there, we had to have about an hour in the air for a whistle every Friday night. And the people on the front, all that neighborhood up around there, wide end colored,…

items.title: Earl Humphrey Interview, 1968-11-30
items.q: other than playing around with my grandfather, you know, giving concerts, churches, and different things like that

ctx.x: Well, let's talk a little bit about your very early days of the band. What were the very, very first jobs you played?

Well, the first jobs I played, I played with a fellow named Dan. He was a guitar player. And he used to have a four-piece band, go out on the lake on Sundays. That was most of his work. Every Sunday he'd have a departure train that was lit up at little, uh, uh, places out there that was dancing. You know, what they called, uh, regular dancing places, you know, camps. You know, camps, you know, out in the water, about, some of them out there about, probably a block of air. Go out on the run, man, and porch all…
What sort of music would that play?
